@Terence Tao and I are pleased to announce the "Prime Number Theorem and Beyond" project, which you can find here:

https://github.com/AlexKontorovich/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd

with blueprint here:

https://alexkontorovich.github.io/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/web/index.html

and dedicated Zulip stream here: #PrimeNumberTheorem+

The initial goal is to get the Prime Number Theorem formalized in Lean (of course it's been done a few times in other systems), and we have three different approaches in mind, the last of which will get the classical exp-root-log error rate. Of course we'll then want to generalize to Dirichlet's theorem, and eventually to Chebotarev.

It turns out that the complex analysis required for these is largely already in place (see, e.g. #9598) and just needs to be developed further (as described in more detail in the blueprint). A trivial yet key observation is that it suffices to work just with rectangles (for which @Yury G. Kudryashov has proved Cauchy's theorem), since rectangles tile one another (unlike discs!). So there's no need for ugly keyhole contours that would be a nightmare to formalize. (Thanks to @Vincent Beffara, discussions with whom led to this observation.)

Thanks also to @Kevin Buzzard, @David Loeffler, @Heather Macbeth, and @Michael Stoll for many comments and suggestions while this project was getting underway (especially Michael's "Euler Products" project which is essential), and @Ian Jauslin for all the technical support with blueprint!
Great project! Further discussion should happen at #PrimeNumberTheorem+.
